title: Granular concurrency shepherd and burst probation policy
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a per-tenant concurrency shepherd and a burst probation policy to reduce noisy neighbor throttles and smooth immediate capacity bursts. Adds telemetry for probation metrics and a lightweight admission controller for Dedicated pools.
description:
Motivation: Dedicated pools occasionally suffer from short, high-amplitude bursts from tenants that overwhelm local warm pools and trigger aggressive preemption. Previous approaches either punished immediately (hard cutoffs) or increased headroom (costly). This PR introduces a probation-based soft-path: an adaptive concurrency shepherd that tracks short-window entropy and enforces a probabilistic admission throttle during a short probation window. The goal is to allow short, well-behaved bursts to pass while automatically dampening pathological spike patterns without long-lived throttles.

What this change does (high level): 1) Concurrency Shepherd: a lightweight per-tenant circuit in the reconcilers that allocates a small soft-concurrency quota and dynamically scales it using a moving-entropy score (variance-aware). It prefers transient allowance over immediate eviction and uses exponential backoff on repeated violations. 2) Burst Probation Policy: when a tenant exceeds its soft-concurrency quota, we enter a probation window (configurable, default 30s). Within probation the tenant is allowed a reduced admission probability rather than an immediate reject; repeated violations escalate to short preemptible reservations. 3) Telemetry and SLO indicators: new Prometheus metrics and tracing spans (probation_entered, probation_score, shepherd_slots, probation_escalations) and a dashboard template for per-tenant probation churn and short-tail P95 latency during probation. 4) Admission Controller: an admission shim implemented in the gateway and dedicated scheduler hook to enforce probabilistic admission with fast-path bypass for pinned/enterprise tenants. 5) Backwards compatible config: feature flag gated, tunable via DedicatedPoolSpec (warmup_fraction, probation_seconds, entropy_threshold, backoff_multiplier).

Commits summary: - a3b7f12: initial shepherd scaffolding and probation state machine - 9d0c2a5: admission shim + gateway integration (probabilistic pass-through) - 47f9c3d: telemetry labels, Prometheus exporters and dashboard JSON - e112a7b: reconciler updates for per-tenant soft quotas and exponential backoff logic - 2f4d9e0: unit & integration tests for probation transitions and fairness under contention

Files changed (high-level): - pkg/autoscaler/shepherd.go (concurrency state machine, entropy calculator) - pkg/autoscaler/probation_policy.go (policy config + transitions) - internal/gateway/admission_probabilistic.go (gateway admission shim) - controllers/dedicatedpool_controller.go (reconcile: attach shepherd to pool) - telemetry/prometheus/probation_metrics.go (metrics and labels) - ui/dashboards/probation_overview.json (Grafana template) - test/integration/probation_scenario_test.go - docs/operating/dedicated_probation.md - charts/redwood-dedicated/values.yaml (defaults)

Design notes and rationale: - Entropy score: we compute a short-window coefficient of variation across concurrency and token-rate to detect erratic bursts vs steady growth. This prevents penalizing legitimate sustained traffic. - Probation over hard cut: many customers observed functional errors when tokens were immediately dropped during brief spikes. Probation provides a probabilistic smoothing that keeps request success rates higher while still protecting shared pools. - Backoff/escalation: escalation paths are capped and time-limited to avoid starvation; we favor short preemptible reservations rather than long-term evictions. - Observability-first: we expose probation churn metrics to enable tuning before enabling in production.
